quarterly_data.signal: CFO Olivier Leonetti on Q4 2025: organic growth was 9% (almost 12% excluding weakness in vehicle and e-mobility); quarterly revenue of $7.1 billion; segment margins expanded 20 basis points to 24.9% (a Q4 record); adjusted EPS of $3.33 up 18%, in line with the guidance midpoint. CEO Paulo Ruiz Sternadt: record revenue and record segment profit; book-to-bill for the combined segments above 1.2 on a quarterly basis (1.1 rolling twelve-month); 2025 organic growth 8%. Electrical Global: total growth 10%, organic 6% (strength in data center, residential and machine OEM), operating margin 19.7% (up 200 basis points), orders up 6% rolling twelve-month with exceptional data-center strength, backlog up 19% YoY. Combined electrical sector: Q4 organic growth 12%, segment margin 26.5%, rolling twelve-month orders up 13%, quarterly orders up more than 40%, total electrical backlog up 29% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $7.1 billion; organic growth 9%; segment margins 24.9%; adjusted EPS $3.33 (18%)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Paulo Ruiz Sternadt on data-center demand: Q4 data-center orders accelerated approximately 200% and data-center sales were up above 40% versus Q4 2024; using Q4 as a proof point, Electrical Americas [data-center] orders grew 200% and orders in Europe grew almost 80% year over year. In 2025 the data-center business grew 44% (49% in Americas, 36% in global) versus an industry forecast of about 33%; the March long-term plan included only 17% data-center growth, which he called by far the biggest upside to the plan. Mix shift: 2025 data-center orders were fifty-fifty cloud vs AI, while 2025 revenues were still 70% cloud and 30% AI; Eaton's dollar-per-megawatt content increases with AI load. Customer base is now balanced: a few years ago a couple of hyperscalers carried most of the weight, today Eaton is 'very well positioned with all hyperscalers and the key multitenant' (no breakdown given); multitenant and new cloud players are more active than he has ever seen, and hyperscalers reconfirmed their 2026 CapEx plans.
quarterly_data.figure: DC orders approximately 200%; DC sales above 40%; 2025 DC growth 44% (49% Americas, 36% global); 2025 revenues 70% cloud / 30% AI

quarterly_data.signal: Electrical Americas Q4 (CFO): organic sales growth of 15% (total growth around 20% per the CEO) driven primarily by data centers, up about 40%, plus commercial and institutional; record operating profit but operating margin of 29.8%, down 180 basis points YoY largely on capacity ramp cost. Orders up 16% on a trailing twelve-month basis (from up 7% in Q3); quarterly orders up more than 18% sequentially and more than 50% YoY; all-time record orders booked in 2025; book-to-bill 1.2; backlog grew by over $3 billion or 31% YoY to $13.2 billion. Negotiations pipeline up to nearly $10 billion in 2025 (over four times 2019, 26% multiyear CAGR); utility orders up low teens on a twelve-month basis. On contract terms, asked by an analyst about five-year hyperscaler supply agreements, the CEO said the multiyear dynamic seen some years ago, when customers bought 'on a panic to guarantee capacity', is no longer happening: orders now deliver in between twelve and eighteen months and 'no one is pre-booking or preordering capacity'.
quarterly_data.figure: organic growth 15%; data centers about 40%; margin 29.8%; backlog $13.2 billion (31%); book-to-bill 1.2; negotiations nearly $10 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO annual mega-project update: mega-project backlog up 30% YoY to $3 trillion across 866 tracked projects; data centers drive most of the growth at 54% of year-to-date announcements (the rest largely U.S. reshoring). The U.S. large data-center construction backlog is now up to eleven years at 2025 build rates, with the U.S. backlog at 206 gigawatts; the project start rate increased slightly to approximately 16%. Eaton's mega-project revenue grew more than 30% in 2025; these projects typically convert to revenue over three to five years ('A market that will be stronger for longer'). In Q&A: industry data-center announcements were up over 200% YoY in 2025, the backlog was also over 200% up (still eleven years of 2025 build) and project starts were up almost 100% YoY.
quarterly_data.figure: US DC backlog 206 gigawatts = eleven years of 2025 builds; mega-project backlog $3 trillion (866 projects); DC 54% of announcements; start rate 16%

quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 guidance: end-market growth assumptions equate to about 7% (commercial aerospace raised to strong double-digit, residential now flat); total-company organic growth 7% to 9% with Electrical Americas at 10% at the midpoint; segment margins 24.6% to 25% (up 30 basis points at the midpoint); adjusted EPS $13 to $13.50 ($13.25 midpoint, up 10%); cash flow $3.9 billion to $4.3 billion (up 14% at the midpoint); no share buybacks in 2026 due to the pending Boyd deal. Q1 2026: organic growth 5% to 7% and operating margins 22.2% to 22.6%, weighed by higher-than-typical capacity ramp-up costs with improvement each quarter; EPS split roughly 44% first half / 56% second half (vs a ten-year average of 47/53; two points from a first-half tax rate of 20 to 21% vs 16 to 17% in the second half, one point from the Electrical Americas ramp). Electrical Americas margin guidance 30% at the midpoint in 2026 and a 32% target by 2030. March long-term plan (6-9% growth, 28% segment margins in 2030, 12% or higher EPS growth): management sees clear upside (data-center growth, acquisitions, mobility spin) but will not refresh 2030 targets yet and plans no Investor Day in 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 organic growth 7% to 9%; adjusted EPS $13.25 midpoint (10%); segment margins 24.6% to 25%; cash flow $3.9 billion to $4.3 billion; Q1 organic 5% to 7%

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity ramp: around $1.5 billion of announced investments across around two dozen (24) projects to expand Electrical Americas capacity. Half finished construction by mid-2025 and started ramping in the second half (mostly Q4), continuing to ramp in 2026; construction of half of the remaining projects will be largely done by the first half of 2026 with ramp starting at the end of the first half; the last quarter of projects continues through 2026 with production ramp in 2027. Second-half 2025 orders were 41% higher than 2024, so Eaton accelerated the ramp (bringing people and resources in earlier), which pressured Q4 2025 and Q1 2026. CFO: ramp costs hit Electrical Americas margin by about 100 basis points in 2025 and about 130 basis points in 2026, front-end loaded (most in Q1 and Q2), with segment margin still about 30%. CEO modeling cadence: Q1 = guidance, progress in Q2, momentum into Q3, then a stronger pace of backlog liquidation in Q4 and into 2027; tiger teams deployed at critical sites, partner network and supply chain scaled for material availability.
quarterly_data.figure: $1.5 billion across 24 projects; ramp margin impact about 100 basis points (2025) and about 130 basis points (2026); last projects ramp in 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on liquid cooling and the pending Boyd acquisition: liquid cooling is growing faster than the data-center average; Eaton's accessible market is already $2.9 million per megawatt with the current portfolio and rises to $3.4 million per megawatt once Boyd is completed. Eaton plays in the inner loop (cold plates, coolant distribution units/CDUs, piping, manifolds, control units) that cools GPUs, TPUs, CPUs, power supplies and network switches, and does not participate in chillers directly (partners with specialized chiller leaders). On the latest NVIDIA announcement that next-generation chips can run hotter, implying operators may need fewer or less powerful chillers ('this still needs to be proven'), he said there is 'no negative impact on the inner loop' - 'quite the opposite', as new systems require more sophisticated cold plates and CDUs. Boyd has about 500 engineers and early technical engagement across all chip platforms and hyperscale plans; after a very solid 2025 finish and a very strong January, Boyd is positioned to meet or exceed 2026 revenues of $1.7 billion. 2025 portfolio moves totaled $13 billion in announced investments (FiberBond, Resilient Power Systems, UltraPCS, Boyd).
quarterly_data.figure: $2.9 million per megawatt today; $3.4 million per megawatt after Boyd; Boyd to meet or exceed 2026 revenues of $1.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the 800-volt DC transition: Eaton is 'leading the technology here with resilient power'; it is working with authorities to create the codes needed to commercialize the technology and has 'a seat at the table to define those codes' together with industry leaders; 'We are ready to make that shift' and is partnering with chip manufacturers and hyperscalers to design their new setups. The Resilient Power acquisition 'accelerates our future towards this direct current technology', and the Fiberbond acquisition 'has been very successful with models built out for the data centers'. Eaton's data-center portfolio spans white-space products around the chip, gray-space power distribution and power quality, and front-of-meter utility grid products.
